proposed.law: For a well-formed context-free grammar in strict nonempty Chomsky normal form with distinct productions A→terminal or A→B C and a finite nonempty input token sequence, return an exact nonnegative integer equal to the number of distinct ordered labelled derivation trees rooted at designated start symbol. Each terminal production A→t accounts for one leaf, each binary production A→B C and split k contributes the product of independently counted left and right trees. Sum all valid alternatives. Inadmissible/duplicate production records, missing nonterminal names, empty input, epsilon/unit productions are rejected rather than silently normalized.
proposed.result: exact nonnegative integer; 0=no parse, 1=unique derivation tree, >1=ambiguous token-sequence parse
proposed.arguments: (grammar:{start,nonterminals:set,terminal_rules:set of (A,t),binary_rules:set of (A,B,C)}, tokens: nonempty finite sequence of terminal symbols)
falsifiers: A boolean recognition result replaces the count and cannot distinguish 2 from 14.
Counting distinct grammar rule orderings as separate trees or collapsing distinct binary derivations into one violates integer ambiguity.
A recursive epsilon cycle is silently accepted in strict CNF: this is outside the defined finite positive grammar.
Returning a float or capped integer for ambiguous input violates exactness.
Double-counting the same production listed twice is invalid: grammar is a set, duplicates must be rejected.

dedup.exact_name_check: No exact name in current 635 D10 selected, D1-D9 contains JSON-PARSE and UNIFY; only a preliminary name filter.
dedup.behavioral_open: A generic semiring chart parser, existing list recursion or dynamic programming can derive this as a self-hosted library. Need proof of an independently justified language-visible D10 root versus a library projection.

proposed.provenance_note: Original Younger (1967) explicitly documents returning an integer representing ambiguity; the exact grammar-validation and empty-input convention below are new SENS proposal conventions, not claims of literal Younger code.

derived_and_hold.law: result > 1 for the exact parse count.
result > 0 for the exact parse count.

derived_and_hold.reason: Chart cells and pointers are implementation/witness structures, not yet a separate semantic root.
Panini rules and Sanskrit morphology are not automatically reducible to a plain strict CNF context-free grammar; do not claim full semantics.
Do not confuse language runtime D2 binary structure parsing with data-level CFG derivation counting.
Epsilon/unit rules and potential infinitely many derivations require separate normalization and occurrence-count preservation proofs.
